key_insight: Uncertainty measures can act as a practical proxy for whether diffusion-generated medical images are semantically correct, not just visually realistic.
clinical_relevance: For NCCT-to-CECT synthesis, uncertainty could help filter unreliable outputs, support quality control, and flag out-of-distribution cases before images are used clinically.
method: Compared six uncertainty approaches: Ensemble, HyperDiff, BayesDiff, MCDropout, RDS, and TTA.
Used AortaDiff to jointly generate CECT images and lumen segmentations so segmentation error could quantify anatomical correctness.
Evaluated uncertainty at pixel, region, and image levels, plus on clinically relevant OOD detection tasks.
evidence_signal: Across internal and external multi-centre data, uncertainty was informative at multiple spatial scales and remained useful under distribution shift, with MCDropout performing strongly and requiring no extra training cost when dropout is already present.
watch_item: Uncertainty was better at identifying severe failures than distinguishing among already high-quality images, so it should complement—not replace—other quality checks.
paper_title: Uncertainty as a Proxy for Semantic Correctness in Diffusion-Based Medical Image Synthesis
